question: Which metal pair starts to melt at room temperature?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gallium and cesium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Gallium** has a melting point of about 29.76°C (85.57°F), which is slightly above room temperature.
 
• **Cesium** has a melting point of about 28.5°C (83.3°F), which is also close to room temperature.
 
• Both metals are unique in that they can exist in liquid form at temperatures near or slightly above typical room temperature.
 
• Gallium is often used in electronics and semiconductors, while cesium is used in atomic clocks and various scientific applications.
 
• The combination of their low melting points makes them interesting for various applications in science and technology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Room Temperature Definition**

 
 
• Room temperature is generally considered to be around 20-25°C (68-77°F).
 
• It is the temperature range within which humans feel comfortable and it is commonly used in scientific studies as a standard.
 
 
 
• **Melting Point**
 
 
• The melting point is the temperature at which a solid becomes a liquid at normal atmospheric pressure.
 
• It is a physical property that is specific to each substance and is used to identify and characterize materials.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Gallium**
 
 
• Used in electronics, particularly in semiconductor technology.
 
• Employed in the production of alloys with low melting points.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Cesium**
 
 
• Used in atomic clocks, which are the most accurate timekeeping devices.
 
• Applied in various scientific research fields and in the oil industry for drilling fluids.
